newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end at tenth consecutive record.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end at tenth consecutive record.

text.p: Swiss shares showed no signs of slowing down, posting the tenth closing record in a row but slightly off the day's highest levels above 4,450 points on the blue-chip SMI.

Dealers said the lack of an alternative to shares and a steady flow of funds made further gains likely. The bourse profited from bullish bond and U.S. markets as well as the firming tendency in the U.S. dollar.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 35.7 points, or 0.81 percent, at 4,444.1. The all-time high was at 4,452.0.
All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 18.25 points, or 0.65 percent, to 2,826.29.
Dealers said shares rallied across the board but that most foreign investors preferred blue chips.
Nestle, UBS and insurer Zurich showed notable gains.

Nestle, up 31 francs to 1,615, was reportedly underpinned by favourable figures from competitor Unilever. Unilever's plans to concentrate on its core activities also sparked hopes that Nestle may spin off part of its business.
UBS bearers were up 32 francs to 1,275 and Zurich added nine francs to 428 on technical factors and recommendations.
CS Group was slightly higher while SBC yielded 0.5 francs to 274.5.
Most-active Novartis registered shares were unchanged at 1,742. Roche were up 95 to 12,470 francs.
ABB, Sulzer and Holderbank also firmed.

Stocks of Alusuisse, which were already hit on Tuesday, were among the losers of the day, giving up 24 francs or two percent to 1,177. The company on Tuesday announced an eight percent rise in 1996 group net profit to 417 million francs, under market expectations.
